title: Part Thirteen: Settled, Contested and Open

sections.brief: What the record settles about Greater Israel 1898-2026, in four classes: documented programmes stated or legislated by named actors (Revisionist both banks; 1967 manifesto; Gush Emunim; Likud 1977 and 2017; Jerusalem and Golan laws; Nation-State Law clause 7; 2022 guidelines and coalition clause; 2019-25 annexation track, Smotrich 82%, Knesset votes); patterns (settling where claimed, withdrawing under pressure or treaty elsewhere, the 2024-26 buffer belt, maps uncorrected); argument (intent beyond stated aims; Nile-to-Euphrates as programme); myths and misreadings (Part Ten ledger and the volume's corrections). Figures: compare (Settled / Contested / Open); time (1898-2026 arc)

What remains open as of 21 October 2026 (the 27 Oct election and the annexation track; E1; Lebanon, Syria and Gaza zones; UNIFIL's end; Temple Mount practice; Golan recognitions; what could not be checked); the central question answered by territory and named actor (West Bank and Golan documented programmes; buffer zones held with security rationales, intent contested; Sinai and east bank no programme; Nile-to-Euphrates no government programme), with the counter-record and the critics' reply. Figure: compare (by territory: stated aim / legal act / on the ground / verdict)
